title: Spatial Information Industry Promotion Institute says suspected personal data leak followed unauthorized access to its website
date_note: Boannews reports the institute's notice (25 November) saying it identified signs of the leak after unauthorized access on the 24th.
geo_basis: country as the source states it; no city given
summary: Boannews reports that the Spatial Information Industry Promotion Institute, a body under South Korea's land ministry, posted a notice saying it identified signs of a suspected personal data leak after unauthorized access on 24 November. Names, mobile phone numbers and email addresses collected through its website may be affected. The institute says it is still determining whether data was leaked, and has put the site on a limited temporary page.
plain: A South Korean public institute says unauthorized access to its website may have leaked names, phone numbers and emails. It is still checking whether data was actually taken.
exec: The institute says it is still determining whether data was leaked and which items were affected, and will publish details after an investigation by relevant authorities.
action: No action needed; for awareness. The institute says it will publish details and corrective measures after the investigation.

validation.note: One publisher (Boannews) quoting the institute's own notice; the notice itself was not opened.

review.note: Compared date 24 Nov, data items, status, temporary page against Boannews
